exceptions.rationale: These three preview tests assert on upstream release.yml steps that the fork's release seam does not provide; they cannot pass without out-of-scope release changes. They stay deleted until B13 reconciles the release seam. The scripts and workflows they cover are restored.

Discord release notifications post to pingdotgg's Discord webhook, which the fork does not hold. Deletions are intentional; the rest of the upstream npm/release pipeline is restored by A2 under fork ownership.
AUR packaging publishes pingdotgg's t3code-bin packages under credentials the fork does not hold. Deletions are intentional.

Upstream maintainer vouch and triage infrastructure (VOUCHED.td, TRIAGE_EXEMPTIONS.td, pr-vouch workflow, contribution-triage skill) is out of scope for a solo-maintained fork per AGENTS.md. Deletions are intentional.

Upstream-internal macroscope review agent configuration was dropped from the fork; fork CI does not run macroscope. Deletions are intentional; the test-signal eval suite they referenced is restored by A2.
The Linux metainfo file is renamed to the fork's app id (com.t3tools.t3code.plusplus). A2 must not restore the upstream path; A5 and A7 must treat the fork path as the seam, not the upstream one.

The only ++ contract data dual-written next to the typed plusplus sidecar carrier are the four released legacy seam groups: SEAM-185 contextBridge on ServerSettings and its patch, SEAM-181 startedAt on PendingBackgroundTask, SEAM-182 monetaryUsage on ServerProviderUsageLimits, and SEAM-183 usageAccounts on ServerProvider. Released clients and stored payloads read those fields directly, so writers keep emitting them while sidecar-first reads prefer the typed carrier. All future ++ data must be sidecar-only; no new direct ++ fields may be added to upstream structs.
